Tesla is finally handing over the first of its all-electric Semi trucks to customers after nearly a decade of delays and refinements to the vehicle, which it first revealed in 2017.
Company executives — except CEO Elon Musk, who was at President Trump’s state dinner with Chinese Premier Xi Jinping — walked an audience of customers, employees, and influencers through many of the details at an event in Reno, Nevada, on Thursday night.
Customers will be able to take delivery of the truck whenever they are ready, though charging infrastructure remains a hurdle, a person familiar with the matter told TechCrunch on the condition of anonymity.
Without revealing the final sticker price, the executives promised the truck will help fleet owners lower their total cost of ownership, reduce emissions, and benefit from greater reliability.
The event was held at a new factory dedicated to the Semi that’s adjacent to the company’s first Gigafactory in Reno. Tesla plans to build as many as 50,000 trucks a year at the plant, or roughly 1,000 per week, and create 3,000 jobs for the local economy. The most capable version of the truck is expected to travel 500 miles or more on one charge (depending on the size of the load) and cost just shy of $300,000 before incentives. There will be shorter-range variants, too.
The Semi’s long-awaited launch comes at a time of transition for Tesla. Musk now paints Tesla as a robotics and AI company even though nearly all of its revenue comes from vehicle sales. He has also changed Tesla’s mission to “build a world of amazing abundance.” When he showed off the Semi in 2017, Tesla’s mission was still “to accelerate the world’s transition to sustainable energy.”
Despite the change in positioning, and seemingly priorities for Tesla, Thursday’s event still saw a lot of discussion about reducing trucking emissions. Dan Priestley, the head of Tesla’s Semi program, noted that heavy trucks produce 16% of emissions despite making up just 1% of vehicles on the road.
“We’re super excited to be deploying these into our own operations because it’s fulfilling the mission that we originally started out [with],” he said.
Originally slated to go into production in 2019, the Semi was delayed for multiple reasons. The pandemic, a global parts supply and semiconductor shortage, and changes made in response to pilot customer feedback all contributed to the years-long wait.
Priestley and Lars Moravy, who leads most of Tesla’s engineering efforts, detailed many of those changes during the 30-minute event — timed thus to show a Semi that started at 3% battery go up to 60% while plugged into one of Tesla’s megawatt charging stations. (Tesla is also building an entire network of these chargers, which Priestley detailed during the event.)
Some of these changes are big and obvious: The company has shaved off roughly 1,000 pounds of weight from the vehicle compared to its original version. Others are more specific, like going from using three different oils in the Semi’s drive axle to just one.
Moravy said the previous axle design that needed three different oils had “always frustrated” him, and admitted that Tesla tends to prioritize “super bespoke” designs. Priestley added that changes to the motor design and work from Tesla’s lubricants team allowed the company to cut out the other two oils. “Occasionally we get a little too far out there,” he said.
Tesla also had to pivot to fix issues with the side windows. In its original design, the company employed pop-out windows that didn’t fully open, and for years, everyone from actual truck drivers to automotive bloggers raised this as an obvious problem.
On Thursday, Priestley offered a mea culpa. He called the original design “not sufficient” and revealed that the new Semi now has standard roll-down windows.
“We fully admit we were wrong about the windows,” he said. “Turns out there’s a lot of infrastructure in the world, whether it’s a badge reader, or your toll booth, or you’re talking to somebody on a call box. There’s all kinds of stuff right at that height, and it became evident that we needed a roll-down window in order to make that infrastructure easier to interface with.”
“It’s okay to be wrong, Dan,” Moravy added.
But Tesla appears to have been right with its goal of making a truck that travels 500 miles on a single charge while fully loaded.
That claim, which Musk made during the original event in 2017, was a source of much derision for years. One of his highest-profile doubters was Bill Gates, who wrote in a 2020 blog post that electric big rigs would “probably never be a practical solution” because “batteries are big and heavy.”
Without naming him, Moravy and Priestley poked fun at Gates onstage during Thursday’s event: “We’re kind of ruthless about every watt-hour that we chase in these things, because there’s this wonderful compounding effect, [which] is that if you make the vehicle more efficient, that means it’s less battery you need to do the same amount of work, which means that you can take battery out of the vehicle, which is lower cost and lower mass,” Priestley said.
“We had some naysayers, names shall not be mentioned,” Moravy followed.
“But, pretty well-known names,” Priestley responded.
“And at Tesla, we love when people tell us something’s impossible. So we took that challenge,” Moravy said.
While Musk was missing, he did pre-tape a segment that ran before the event started. In the video, he said the Semi will be the “funnest truck to drive.” He also promised Tesla’s partial automation features (curiously missing from the Semi despite the years of delays) will be added in the “near future.”
Musk also pitched the truck as making “a ton of sense economically, because the cost of electricity per mile is much less than the cost of diesel, especially in these crazy times” — though that final clause conveniently glosses over the fact that diesel prices have shot up because the president Musk himself helped elect has started a war that’s roiled energy markets.

Ed Sheeran's concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday have been cancelled because of severe weather warnings in the area.
The singer had been scheduled to perform two shows at the Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, near Boston, as part of his current US tour.
The tour has been in the headlines because of a row over a decision to drop Sheeran's support act Macklemore for making pro-Palestinian comments on stage. Stadium owners including the Gillette Stadium's Robert Kraft lobbied for his removal.
A statement from the venue said: "Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, the promoter and tour have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium."
It added: "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority.
"Refunds are available now at the point of purchase. Ticketholders who purchased through Ticketmaster will be automatically refunded."
Weather warnings for high winds are in force in the area until the early hours of Sunday, and officials have told drivers to minimise travel.
Sheeran was at the eye of a very different storm last week after the decision to drop Macklemore from his tour.
The decision came after the rapper made on-stage comments at earlier concerts including calling for "free Palestine" and referring to "genocide" in Gaza, as well as showing images of Gaza.
Kraft, who is Jewish, accused the US rapper of hate speech and said Macklemore would not be allowed to appear at the Gillette Stadium, the home of his New England Patriots American football team.
Sheeran said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoter, not by him. The promoter said venue owners including Kraft would have refused to let the concerts take place if Macklemore was on the bill.
Macklemore's removal from the tour led Sheeran's other support and backing artists to pull out in protest, and sparked a heated debate over free speech and the role of politics in music.
Returning to the stage last weekend, Sheeran told fans he "had to take and make difficult decisions - and I am making mistakes - and I'm so, so sorry".

articles.title_orig: China swimmer makes Asian Games history as Thai sprinter wins track 100m
articles.title_zh: China swimmer makes Asian Games history as Thai sprinter wins track 100m
articles.content_orig:
Towering teenager Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer in history to win seven golds at a single Asian Games, while on the track, Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson powered to victory in the 100m.
China’s Zhang, 19, scorched to the men’s 400m freestyle title in the pool in Tokyo on Friday in a Games-record three minutes and 41.28 seconds.
He sat on the lane divider after the race and slowly counted off on his fingers all seven medals he had won.
Zhang also won individual golds in the 200m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle events, as well as three relays.
He said, after wrapping up a scintillating campaign, that it had been the “perfect week”.
“I think the most important thing is to stay grounded and focused, because the Asian Games are not my ultimate goal,” said Zhang, who stands 198cm (six feet, six inches).
With the Los Angeles Olympics less than two years away, China won 30 of the 42 golds in the pool this week.
Their 13-year-old phenomenon Yu Zidi was the undoubted superstar, taking home three individual golds and all in Games-record times.
Not to be outdone, Japan’s 17-year-old Shin Ohashi shattered the men’s 200m breaststroke world record on Thursday.
Swimming, equestrian and diving are taking place in Tokyo, but the city of Nagoya and the wider Aichi prefecture are the main Games host.
The men’s and women’s 100m sprints, the blue riband events in track and field, took place in front of rows of empty seats in Nagoya.
China’s Chen Yujie streaked to a comfortable victory in the women’s final in a Games-record 11.06 seconds.
The men’s was won by 20-year-old Puripol, who burst out of the pack in the final quarter of the race to win in 9.90 seconds, breaking his Games record from earlier in the evening.
It was Thailand’s first men’s 100m gold medal since Suchart Jairsuraparp on home soil at the 1978 Bangkok Games.
On the last evening of gymnastics, Carlos Yulo won the men’s vault for his second gold of the Games.
The double Olympic champion won floor gold on Thursday to complete his collection of major titles.
“I can’t believe it,” the Filipino said.
“In this whole Asian Games, I felt really stressed, but at the same time, I enjoyed what I did today. I really did my part.
“Today was really a miracle for me.”
There’s little time to celebrate, however, with the world championships next month.
South Korea edged China 85-80 in the semifinals of the women’s basketball, and will face hosts Japan for gold.
China had their giant centre Zhang Ziyu, 19, but it was not enough.
Zhang Ziyu stands 223cm (seven feet, four inches) and scored 22 points.
“She was tough to guard,” said South Korea’s Kang Lee-seul.
“We couldn’t defend her, but we focused on fast breaks and shooting more three-pointers.”
North Korea’s women were again in record-setting form on the weightlifting dais.
Oh Kwang Ok set three world records on her way to women’s 57kg bodyweight class gold.
Oh lifted 104kg in the snatch and 134kg in the clean and jerk for a 238kg total – all world records to add to the two golds North Korea’s women won in the 49kg and 53kg classes this week.
North Korea has won four gold medals and two silvers in the six weightlifting events contested so far.

Ed Sheeran’s concerts scheduled for this weekend at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts have been canceled due to severe weather, amid wider turmoil surrounding the British pop star’s tour.
The concerts scheduled for Friday and Saturday at the New England Patriots home stadium were scrapped because of the upcoming nor’easter , Messina Touring, Sheeran’s touring group, said in an Instagram statement.
“Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium,” the statement said. “The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority.”
The touring group said that refunds are available and that ticket holders who purchased through Ticketmaster will be automatically refunded.
The announcement comes amid a wider scandal for Sheeran’s “Loop” tour since one of its opening acts was forced out for voicing pro-Palestinian views.
Earlier this month, rapper Macklemore said he was removed from Sheeran’s tour after speaking out in support for the Palestinian people at the tour’s shows in New Jersey. Macklemore said he was removed at the behest of New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft and alleged that Kraft organized a boycott among stadium owners.
Kraft did not immediately return a request for comment. In a previous statement he said he did not intend to stifle Palestinian support but to ensure a “welcoming environment” at Gillette Stadium.
Macklemore’s removal prompted Sheeran’s other opening acts — Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham, Finneas and his house band, Beoga — to withdraw in protest.
A rep for Sheeran did not immediately return a request for comment. In his first concert since the scandal, Sheeran apologized for the scenario.
“I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician,” Sheeran said, “but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.”
On Thursday, Macklemore announced a Free Palestine Tour for this fall.
The multiday nor’easter is expected to hit the East Coast, affecting states from Virginia to Rhode Island. Coastal flood alerts are in effect for 33 million people. Wind gusts are expected to peak on Saturday, reaching up to 60 mph in coastal locations.

Sheeran has since been accused of 'bowing to the mob' after he apologized to his fans for his handling of the row.

An early-season nor'easter will bring coastal flooding, high surf, strong winds and rain to parts of the East Coast through the weekend, with impacts from North Carolina to New England.
New York City and especially Boston need to stay weather aware this weekend, and prepare the same as you would for a tropical storm.
The nor'easter is strengthening as it heads north. The map below shows the winds and rain as the low moves north along the East Coast.
Wind gusts over 30 mph, with occasional gusts from 40 to 50 mph, are occurring along the coast from southeast New England to the Outer Banks of North Carolina.
( MORE: Nor'easter tracking maps )
Coastal flooding is also occurring at high tide from parts of Long Island to North Carolina.

Here's a general timeline of the storm and its impacts over the next several days.
The map below shows coastal flood alerts have been issued by the National Weather Service. These alerts include Atlantic City, Long Island, the Norfolk metro area, Ocean City (Maryland and New Jersey), downtown Boston, Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket.
The most significant coastal flooding will be from the northern Outer Banks of North Carolina to the  Jersey shore, including the Virginia Tidewater, as well as Chesapeake Bay and Delaware Bay.
(WATCH: Nor'easter waves slam stilt homes on the Outer Banks )
This flooding will happen for multiple high tides into the weekend, in these areas. It will also be boosted by Saturday's full moon, with some of the highest astronomical tides of the month.
Given this repeated battering from high surf, beach erosion is expected along stretches of these beaches, potentially reaching extreme levels for some areas.
At least minor coastal high tide flooding will also develop in parts of New England by late Friday into the weekend.
One bit of good fortune with this storm is that its rainfall will be spread out over several days, rather than arriving in one short deluge.
While we expect the most rain to fall from southern New England to New Jersey, those rainfall totals in the map below will be stretched out through Monday.
That means any rainfall flooding should be mainly local in nature in some of the traditional urban trouble spots.
That rainfall could also add to any coastal flooding at high tide through Sunday.
In the New York City metro area, the heaviest rainfall is expected in Long Island, with less rain as you go west into the outer New Jersey suburbs.
High wind warnings are in effect for parts of southeast New England, including Boston and Providence, and also along coasts of Delaware and New Jersey. In these areas, gusts up to 60 mph are possible through Saturday night.
In these areas, some tree damage and power outages are most likely. Ground soaked from the nor'easter's rain, as well as trees still with leaves will only enhance this threat of tree damage and outages.
Otherwise, occasional gusts from 40 to 50 mph are possible from North Carolina's Outer Banks to other parts of coastal New England. Some sporadic power outages and tree limb damage are also possible in these areas.
Here are some tips to keep in mind if you plan to travel to the Northeast into this weekend:

Some gusts topped 40 mph along the coast from southern Massachusetts down to the Virginia Tidewater Wednesday.
And those persistent winds are piled up water from the ocean and bays along parts of the coast.
Minor to moderate coastal flooding was reported from parts of the Jersey Shore to southeast Virginia during Wednesday's morning and evening high tides.
Flooding was reported Wednesday morning in downtown Norfolk, Smithfield and Suffolk, Virginia, according to the National Weather Service.
Widespread gusts of 30-45 mph were ongoing as of Thursday evening, with peak gusts over 45 mph reported along the coast of North Carolina.
Those persistent winds were piling up water from the ocean and bays along parts of the coast. Water levels reached major flood stage during high tide Thursday evening.
A 16-mile stretch of the North Carolina Highway 12 on the Outer Banks is closed in both directions due to ocean overwash. Specifically, the road is closed from Sea Oats Drive to Oregon Inlet Road in Dare County.
Rising waters forced the cancellation of the Oceans Calling festival in Maryland.
You might think it is too early for a nor’easter, but the criteria for a nor’easter are met more often than you would think.
A nor’easter simply means that the winds blow into an area from the northeast. For the Northeast, that usually means an area of low pressure is just off the coast, which brings the winds in this direction.
(More: What is a nor’easter? )
Most people usually think of snow and ice with nor’easters and that is because nor’easters do tend to occur more in the late fall and winter.
The most notable nor’easters tend to bring heavy snow because these lows move up along the Gulf Stream, tapping into the warm ocean. This warm, moist air then clashes with the cold air over the Northeast to create heavy snowfall. Fortunately, this one is occurring way earlier, so it is all rain this time.

articles.title_zh: From Sam Altman to Mark Zuckerberg: All the tech billionaires at the Trump-Xi dinner
articles.content_orig:
American tech billionaires filled the seats at President Trump’s flashy state dinner honoring Chinese leader Xi Jinping Thursday night, as concerns about the global AI race take center stage.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Apple Chairman Tim Cook, and AMD CEO Lisa Su were seen in photos at Trump and Xi’s table, at the very center of the festivities.
The invitees also included Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Greg Brockman, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Alphabet’s Sergey Brin and Sundar Pichai, and Michael Dell of Dell Technologies.
In contrast to a 2015 dinner then-President Barack Obama hosted for Xi, no Chinese business leaders showed up, the Washington Post noted.
Still, the dinner marked a rare opportunity for the most powerful figures in tech to rub elbows with Chinese state dignitaries, as innovators have been divided in a heated debate over whether the world needs to slow development of dangerous AI models or push ahead.
President Trump has shrugged off doomsday warnings about AI’s potential to harm humanity, including one chilling prediction that it could lead to human extinction by 2030 – instead arguing that the more pressing threat is China pulling ahead in the race.
Chinese officials have also dismissed the warnings as “fear mongering” and “Cold War” tactics , urging companies to push ahead with development. Xi has stated that China will take the lead in fostering AI collaboration among developing countries.
Despite rising tensions within the industry, pols and tech figures were all smiles at the elaborate soirée in the East Room of the White House, walking a red carpet on the North Portico steps before the event.
The dinner featured red blossoms and red linens in a nod to the color of China’s flag, a toast of Schramsberg “Blanc De Noir,” and a menu with Chinese influences, all overseen by First Lady Melania Trump.
Notably absent from the dinner was Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, one of the industry leaders who has been most aggressive in calling for more stringent regulations on AI companies – drawing blowback from Trump himself.
Amodei recently published a lengthy essay proposing a three-step plan for global tech giants to slow their development of AI models, after an Anthropic researcher quit his job and sounded the alarm over potential dangers of the technology.
Altman and Musk – longtime rivals who were locked in a messy legal battle earlier this year – each backed Amodei’s proposal, which requires cooperation from regulators and tech companies around the world.
Trump accused Amodei of “pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’” and argued that any slowdown in US development could help China.
“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!” the president wrote in a Truth Social post earlier this month.
Anthropic also butted heads with the government earlier this year when it refused to allow unfettered access to its technology for use in weaponry and mass surveillance.
War Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a blacklisting of the company, though a federal judge later struck down the ban.
Huang, who has been pushing to tap into the massive Chinese market, and Zuckerberg, whose company recently launched a popular AI agent , have each argued that the warnings around AI dangers have been blown out of proportion , saying the matter of development should be left to companies themselves – not regulators.

“This move is a diplomatic all-timer,” Santi Ruiz, a policy-focused writer for the Institute for Progress and editorial team member at AI company Anthropic, posted on X. “It's like Messi cutting inside. You know it’s coming. It doesn’t matter how many times they run it. You’re getting those pandas, and you’ll like it.”
The tried-and-tested offering came once again on Thursday as Chinese President Xi Jinping announced during his state visit to the U.S. that Ping Ping and Fu Shuang , two giant pandas from a research base in Chengdu, would be lent to Zoo Atlanta in the state of Georgia—but whether this so-called panda diplomacy remains as welcome as it has over the decades is less clear, eliciting mixed reactions in 2026.
The practice gained traction after the National Zoo received giant pandas from Beijing in the wake of President Richard Nixon and First Lady Pat Nixon’s historic trip to China in 1972, which marked a new, positive chapter in U.S.-China relations.
China claims ownership of nearly all the giant pandas in the world, even their offspring, and controls who receives them. Beijing eventually shifted from gifting giant pandas to leasing them to other countries in 1984 as the animal’s population dwindled, but the practice continued and spread to other nations like Austria, Canada, and Malaysia. China regularly considers loaning pandas an act of goodwill—even when the host nation typically foots the bill of about $1 million annually for a pair.
A giant panda’s presence or absence in a country tends to represent ebbs and flows of its relationship with China. For instance, amid tensions with Japan over Taiwan , Tokyo returned two giant pandas to Sichuan on loan in January, marking the first time Japan does not have a giant panda since 1972, when China-Japan ties first normalized. In 2010, two U.S.-born panda cubs returned to China , days after Chinese officials warned then-President Barack Obama against meeting the Dalai Lama, whom Beijing considers a separatist.
“No other animal has been turned into a symbol to the extent that pandas have been,” says Czeslaw Tubilewicz, a senior lecturer at Adelaide University.
It’s also no coincidence that Zoo Atlanta received the giant pandas, Tubilewicz says, as the gift represented Beijing’s appreciation of Georgia’s historical economic partnership with China on several aspects: “When most southern states, especially Republican states, turned very negative on China, Georgia continued its pro-China policy consistently. So when it comes to those pandas, and in [Zoo Atlanta], in a way, Xi Jinping is trying to kill two birds with two pandas.”
But China’s transformation from a developing economy to one of the world’s superpowers has also raised questions about whether the gesture of sending giant pandas still works. China is massively different from how it used to be in the 1970s, and is currently embroiled in a wide range of issues, not only with the U.S., but also with other countries, which makes categorizing it neatly as a friend or foe less easy.
Ja Ian Chong, associate professor of political science at the National University of Singapore, tells TIME that “the image of the pandas as soft, friendly, and cuddly—they don’t work today because a lot of [China’s aggressive] actions now are a lot more visible and fresh in people’s minds.”
“No one cares about pandas when national security or geostrategic interests come into play,” Tubilewicz added.
A 2022 peer-reviewed study at the University of Connecticut found that U.S. students who viewed panda videos that were not sourced from the government were likely to have a positive attitude toward Chinese culture and, in turn, Chinese people.
But while China’s practice of leasing pandas gives some people warm feelings, it makes others hot with anger. Conservationists and animal advocates have argued against using pandas as geopolitical pawns. Following the South Korea-China Summit earlier this year, the countries’ respective environmental officials discussed additional giant panda loans. But a Korean animal rights group slammed the move , saying that the creatures “are not beings born for human entertainment or interstate friendship.”
And many others are also starting to look past the panda diplomacy and demand other measures. A 2026 survey of U.S. adults conducted by NORC at the University of Chicago found that 28% of respondents said sending pandas to American zoos would improve their view of China, but much higher percentages said that more concrete actions like Chinese cooperation on curbing fentanyl precursors or easing trade restrictions would improve their view of China.
“The symbolism was still dominant in the 1970s,” Chong said. “It’s just that, given the lack of information, given the environment of that time, the symbolism probably got a lot more traction before than today.”
While surveys show many Americans are warming to China , Chong says “deep reservoirs of reservations remain,” particularly among Trump’s MAGA base: a July survey from the Chicago Council on Global Affairs says that 63% of MAGA Republicans favor limiting the growth of Chinese power.
“Affection for pandas does not automatically translate into support for Chinese government policies,” Yu Tao, associate professor in Chinese Studies at the University of Western Australia, tells TIME. “Its more realistic contribution is to sustain public goodwill and opportunities for cooperation. The strongest case for panda diplomacy is that it gives people something they want to preserve in a relationship otherwise defined pretty much by disputes.”

articles.title_orig: 2026 WNBA Playoffs Primer: Upsets, Chaos, and My Title Pick
articles.title_zh: 2026 WNBA Playoffs Primer: Upsets, Chaos, and My Title Pick
articles.content_orig:
The chaos of the final day of the WNBA regular season, which decided three of the four first-round playoff matchups, feels like a scaled-down harbinger of what’s next. We’re about to see an unusually wide-open first round; the gap between the no. 1 and no. 8 seeds is a historically tight seven games. For reference, that gap was 11 games last season and 17 the season before. Every lower seed boasts a little bit of a “nobody wants to see them in the first round” factor, besides the injury-plagued Dallas Wings, who carry the inferior but still scary “nothing to lose” label.
The WNBA’s 30th regular season has also been its longest, and the home-away-home format of the first round (which isn't organized by conference) will guarantee arduous travel for six of eight playoff teams. To boot, half the league is still getting over the jet lag and interruption caused by the FIBA tournament earlier this month in Berlin, held smack-dab in the final third of the WNBA season. There has never been a better time for an underdog to steal a game—or even a series.
I hesitate to romanticize the WNBA’s shoestring-budget past, but there’s something quaint about a season marked by exponential increases in player salaries hearkening back to the league’s adaptive, provisional roots. In time, the first round will be longer, and once expansion is complete, conferences will likely be reinstated as a structuring part of postseason play. But for now, in the messy middle of the WNBA’s ascendance , we are being given the gift of a rare first round where just about anything could happen—which has both its charms and frustrations.
With that in mind, let’s rank the first-round series based on the likelihood of an upset, starting with the longest shot, and examine the postseason race as a whole.
Paige Bueckers controls the ball against Gabby Williams
Dallas is the great afterthought of the postseason, and rightfully so. It has been absolutely decimated by injuries. Azzi Fudd, the 2026 no. 1 pick and the Wings’ best point-of-attack defender, is out for the rest of the season. The status of Alanna Smith, whose rim protection has carried a team to the WNBA Finals before, remains up in the air.
But they do have two wild cards:
I don’t see Dallas winning this series, but I wouldn’t be surprised if it kept up against the Valkyries’ style longer than expected.
One more stat: Dallas’s new starting lineup has the best offensive rating in the WNBA.
Breanna Stewart, Olivia Miles, and Han Xu go up for a rebound
When Sabrina Ionescu told reporters recently that New York isn’t your traditional eighth seed, she wasn’t just offering feigned optimism. The Liberty defeated the Lynx in five (controversial) games in the 2024 WNBA Finals, and the 26-18 record they clawed their way to this season—despite injuries to Ionescu, Satou Sabally (who is out for the year), Leonie Fiebich, and more—would have been good enough for the no. 5 seed last year.
The Lynx would have been a shoo-in to beat nearly any of the other lower seeds, but they've historically (and recently) struggled against New York's size.
As we found out in their last matchup, Fiebich and Breanna Stewart are one of the only duos with the size, speed, and versatility to switch an Olivia Miles–Napheesa Collier pick-and-roll.
With Collier back in the starting lineup, the Lynx are better as a whole than they were before her return—averaging a plus-18.5 net rating—but Collier adds some subtle wrinkles that could prove advantageous for New York. With Natasha Howard setting the bulk of Miles’s screens, the pick-and-roll had turned into a perpetual layup line for Minnesota. With Collier back, the Lynx have become more jumper-happy, partially because the two-time MVP runner-up gets double-teamed constantly. On its own, adding a little bit of variance to fuel a scintillating offense isn’t a bad thing. But the Lynx are also giving up five more points in the paint than they were before Collier’s return from her ankle surgeries. The five-time All-Star simply isn’t at 100 percent yet—by her own admission—and her gradual return to form has naturally taken a toll on Minnesota’s physicality in the paint, an area where it has to put forth a full-throttle effort to make up for its lack of defensive size.
One more stat: The Lynx are in the bottom three in the WNBA in points in the paint since Collier’s return .
Kiki Iriafen drives to the basket against Angel Reese
Hey, Washington: Get Angel Reese in foul trouble. She is frankly Atlanta’s only line of defense against the Mystics’ three-headed frontcourt monster of Kiki Iriafen, Shakira Austin, and Lauren Betts. The Dream are 7.9 points per 100 possessions worse defensively when Reese sits, and there’s a steep drop-off when her backups, even DeWanna Bonner, enter the game.
The Mystics and the Dream have similar styles. At a time when the rest of the WNBA is trending toward guard play and offense, both are in the top three in defensive rating, points in the paint, second-chance points, and free throw attempts. But in a war of attrition, the team with the most bodies—and, therefore, the most contingency plans—wins, and that’s the Mystics. For the Mystics, the youngest team in the WNBA, this is an opportunity to call shots, take names, form an identity, and prove that they are formidable as well as fun.
One more stat: The Mystics may be ranked 12th on offense, but they have the no. 1 free throw rate in the WNBA.
Caitlin Clark is guarded by A’ja Wilson and Jewell Loyd
The Aces and the Fever have similar makeups: a Big Three, questionable depth made worse by crushing injuries, and maddening defensive inconsistency. The Aces have lost NaLyssa Smith, A’ja Wilson’s frontcourt mate and a legit Most Improved Player candidate, for the season due to a knee injury. The Fever, meanwhile, await potentially devastating news on the status of Ty Harris, who had to be carried off the court in the final game of the regular season because of an ankle injury. Aliyah Boston also left that game early with a leg injury that has hampered her nearly all season long.
With Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, Indiana has the best-scoring backcourt of all time. The Aces, on the other hand, have such putrid perimeter defense that Becky Hammon is starting essentially a one-way player in Stephanie Talbot, who has logged eight zero-point games this season. With Smith out, Hammon will likely have to go small around Wilson, exacerbating the Aces’ defensive issues. Per Synergy, nobody has given up more points as a primary defender this season than the Aces’ Jackie Young. Jewell Loyd, at 11th worst, is not far behind. The Fever have their own perimeter deficiencies on the defensive end, and I wouldn’t blame you for picking the team featuring the GOAT and the title pedigree to win here. But if the series turns into a defense-optional, offense-optimal free-for-all, I’m siding with Indiana, which has broken the 100-point mark this season more than any other team in WNBA history.
One more stat: The Aces’ Big Three of Wilson, Young, and Chelsea Gray have logged 243 games together (postseason included).

On paper, a Fever-Dream rematch featuring Clark versus Reese—with the added juice of Bonner returning to Indiana after leaving the team just five games into last season—should be the stuff of a sportswriter’s dreams. Millions in the Northeast are bracing for a powerful nor'easter set to bring pounding rain and strong winds to the region through the weekend.
The nor'easter could also cause power outages and could spark flight disruptions along the Northeast coast.
The storm has canceled Ed Sheeran's weekend concerts at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts, according to ABC Boston affiliate WCVB. The Global Citizen Festival in New York City and Oceans Calling, a music festival in Ocean City, Maryland, have also been canceled.
Here's the latest forecast:
The storm is bringing massive waves for days, which will cause significant beach erosion.

Waves up to 12 feet are possible from the Outer Banks to the New Jersey shore through Saturday, and along the New England coast through Sunday.
Coastal flood alerts are in effect from the Outer Banks to Maine, as some areas will see flood inundation up to 3 feet above normal levels.
Strong winds are also a major threat as the nor'easter moves north.
The Jersey Shore, Rhode Island and Massachusetts coasts are under a high wind warning from Friday night to Sunday, with dangerous gusts up to 60 mph possible.
The Jersey Shore is under a high wind warning from Friday night to Sunday, with dangerous gusts up to 60 mph possible.
New York City could see wind gusts of 40-to-50 mph Friday night through Sunday.

The storm will reach peak strength on Saturday and then weaken slightly on Sunday as it stalls over New Jersey.
On Sunday, the rain will become more scattered, but still much of the day will be wet from Washington, D.C., to Maine.

articles.title_orig: Over 30 CEOs scored an invite to the US-China state dinner — and these 4 got a spot at the head table
articles.title_zh: Over 30 CEOs scored an invite to the US-China state dinner — and these 4 got a spot at the head table
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
President Trump touted Thursday's long-awaited state dinner at the White House as a tough ticket, and while the Chinese business delegation was notably absent , the glittering event featured a wide array of US CEOs.
The official invite list included more than 30 present or former US CEOs, largely from the technology sector, as well as from banking, carmakers, and pharmaceuticals.
Perhaps most striking were the four CEOs whom Trump's team chose to sit at the head table with the two heads of state.
Elon Musk of Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) was seated next to Melania Trump, while Jensen Huang of Nvidia ( NVDA ), former Apple ( AAPL ) CEO Tim Cook, as well as Lisa Su of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) filled out the head table.
In his remarks before the crowd, Trump said the US and Chinese relationship has been built on a "foundation of commerce and mutual respect between our countries, and together we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations."
The dinner menu, according to the White House, featured three courses to showcase "American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence," including a wild mushroom fricassée, sesame-crusted sea bass, and honey ice cream.
Read more: Tech stocks gain after tech titan dinner with Trump and China's Xi Jinping
The guest list was notable for the outsized presence of tech CEOs and leaders in artificial intelligence. Huang, in particular, has spoken out in recent days against government regulations on the sector, a position Trump has often echoed.
One of the attendees, Satya Nadella of Microsoft, spoke to Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa earlier this week and offered optimism about the overall US-China relationship, saying of AI, "I think both sides will care about the same set of things at the end of the day, which is they want to be able to have this technology actually help their citizens get value." He said safety will be an important element for both sides as norms are set.
The dinner — like many previous Trump events — mixed CEOs among administration officials, Republican party leaders, Fox News hosts, and Supreme Court justices.

articles.title_zh: Details on US, China Trade Talks to Come on Monday, Says Greer
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that the U.S. and China have reached agreements covering a subset of goods the two countries can trade on more favorable terms, marking fresh progress in negotiations between the world's two largest economies.
"We've actually reached agreement with the Chinese on a number of these things," Greer said on CNBC's "Squawk Box," referring to goods including U.S. agricultural products and medical devices and Chinese consumer goods considered non-sensitive.
Greer said the Trump administration plans to release "a lot more details" Monday about what the two sides have accomplished in negotiations over the past several weeks. He said the goal is to carve out areas of trade that could remain insulated from future tariff measures or broader trade disputes.
The two countries want some goods to be traded on a "more preferential basis" and potentially left aside if either country imposes new tariffs.
Greer did not specify Friday which products are covered by the agreements, how tariffs on those goods could change or when the new terms would take effect. Negotiations under the new U.S.-China "Board of Trade" mechanism are focused on "pure trade issues," Greer said, rather than U.S. national security restrictions on advanced technology.
"All those export controls that are national security issues, we take those off the table," Greer said.
Trump and Xi, after they met in Beijing in May, announced the establishment of the "Board of Trade" to manage trade between the two rivals in non-sensitive products. Businesses have been waiting for more details on what categories of trade would be set aside, under the new framework, for lower tariffs.

articles.content_orig:
One of the three attendees who was shot at Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, has passed away from complications stemming from his injuries, according to the Pennsylvania attorney general.
Jim Copenhaver, 76, was struck twice when a gunman opened fire from a nearby rooftop. Another attendee, Corey Comperatore, was killed in the shooting and Trump's ear was grazed by a bullet.
Copenhaver died on Wednesday at a hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, according to a statement from the Allegheny County medical examiner shared with local media.
The gunman, 20-year-old Thomas Crooks, was killed by Secret Service after he opened fire.
In a post on his social media site Truth Social, Trump called Copenhaver a "true American patriot".
"More than two years ago in Butler, Pennsylvania, a crazed gunman attempted to stifle our America First Movement. Instead, Jim and so many other wonderful Patriots who love our Country, stood united in defense of our shared values of Freedom, Liberty, and Justice," Trump said. "Our hearts and prayers are with the Copenhaver family, especially his incredible wife Marianne."
An attorney for Copenhaver's family said his dedication to the US was a "defining part of his life".
"As a veteran, he proudly served our nation in the armed forces, and his love of country never wavered," the lawyer said in a statement to the BBC's US partner CBS News.
In an interview with CBS a year after the Butler rally, Copenhaver and David Dutch, the third attendee who was shot, said they had been through infections and surgeries after being wounded.
Copenhaver was shot in the arm and the abdomen. A year later, the bullet was still lodged in his body next to his spine, he told CBS, causing him to walk with a cane.
Both Dutch and Copenhaver sued the federal government for damages in June, arguing the Secret Service failed to ensure their safety and was therefore liable for their injuries.
Republicans in the US House of Representatives also paid tribute to Copenhaver on Friday, saying in a social media post: "Jim endured unimaginable hardship with strength and perseverance."

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Indexes Tick Higher at Open as Treasury Yields, Oil Prices Pull Back; Nasdaq, S&P 500 on Pace for Weekly Gains
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Indexes Tick Higher at Open as Treasury Yields, Oil Prices Pull Back; Nasdaq, S&P 500 on Pace for Weekly Gains
articles.content_orig:
The bond market is yelling at the Federal Reserve, but the messages are coming from different directions and pose a dilemma for policymakers as they seek to strike a balance that won't tank the economy.
Treasury yields continued their upward march Thursday as investors sought to price in a variety of factors: inflation still hovering well above the Fed's 2% goal, another bump up in energy prices and the impact of a global hyperscaler financial arms race and accompanying debt issuance.
In the past, policymakers have been willing to look through inflation spurts from temporary shocks like high energy prices and tariffs. And the narrative not so long ago was that the artificial intelligence investing boom was a story that would last a year or two and ultimately prove disinflationary.
But now Fed officials are rethinking the impact of those factors and seeing the danger of more durable inflation.
At the same time, markets are grappling with a central bank that suddenly has no interest in telegraphing its next moves, leaving an uncertain calculus on who is calling the shots — policymakers or market players.
"The time of looking through the initial supply shock has come to an end," said Joseph Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM. "The bias has to be towards restoring price stability, and they should take what's going on seriously."
Markets expect the central bank will indeed take a firmer hand on inflation.
Over the past day or so, traders raised the odds of a rate hike in October, which would come only a month or so after last week's quarter percentage point increase . They also see a third increase either late this year or early in 2027, with additional hikes possible in subsequent months.
That's a big switch from a Fed that in June projected it might hike once this year and then be done before starting to cut in the next couple of years.
"My view coming out of the [September] meeting was that we're going to get three rate hikes," Brusuelas said. But modeling performed at his firm about the potential for higher yields, along with a prolonged cycle of AI investment, changed that view.
The modeling indicated that sharply higher long-term yields could slow growth and increase unemployment and still not get inflation back to 2%. RSM found that even a 5.5% 10-year yield — it was around 5.15% on Thursday — would lower growth to 1.5% and lift unemployment to 4.7% while core inflation remained stuck at 2.4%.
"The Fed is underestimating what's going to be necessary to restore price stability — that we're probably not talking two or three hikes. We're talking five or six," Brusuelas said.
Not everyone on Wall Street agrees. Some strategists think the market is getting ahead of itself — that yields now essentially are pricing in stronger economic growth and are overly sensitive to the vagaries of oil prices amid the ongoing tensions in the Middle East.
"The rise in yields has not been due to expectations of a too-dovish Fed allowing inflation to persistently exceed target. Instead, the rise has been in real yields as investors priced-in the Fed setting higher policy rates," Citigroup economist Andrew Hollenhorst said in a note. "It should not be surprising that this has led to both higher shorter-term and longer-term yields."
Indeed, several key Fed officials, while endorsing near-term rate hikes, also are counseling patience.
New York Fed President John Williams , whose position puts him in the vice chair slot of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, said Thursday that it's "reasonable" to expect another hike by the end of the year, but also noted that officials need to keep watching the data before getting on a pre-set "forward guidance" track of locking in rate hikes.
Similarly, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson also indicated additional policy tightening is likely but characterized the potential moves as "modest," hardly an indication that she thinks a string of hikes is likely.
Still, the Fed faces a policy crossroads: Tighten too much and risk cutting off the expansion, or tighten too little and risk losing the market's faith that it is sufficiently tuned into inflation risks.
"Weak guidance guardrails risk putting ... central banks in a position where they may have to decide between a sub-optimal hike and disappointing the market and risking hard-won credibility," Krishna Guha, head of economics and central bank strategy at Evercore ISI, said in a note. "Lack of guidance also means whatever decision they take risks generating an outsized market response — either substantially further tightening or easing market rates."
Guha is in the camp that the market's expectations are "too aggressive" while also seeing the Fed's dilemma.
"Delivering back-to-back hikes — particularly without forward guidance as to how to interpret them — would risk sending a very hawkish signal that would reprice the rates curve further and to an unpredictable extent," Guha said. "But, skipping a hike priced odds-on in the market could also lead to a large repricing in the other dovish direction."
The conflict is critical now because Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has emphasized letting markets help guide policy. That's a big reversal from central bank policy since the global financial crisis in 2008, when the Fed used its forward-guidance tool to signal to investors which way rates were headed.
"His framework appears significantly less rooted in economic measurement details and significantly more reflective of market narratives," UBS economist Jonathan Pingle wrote of Warsh. "No Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve has emphasized considering the signals from financial markets as an input into monetary policy decisions as strongly as Chairman Warsh."
With a yield surge that has taken the 30-year bond to its highest level since 2004, market dynamics have swung Warsh from someone calling for cuts prior to taking the job in May, to a chair who seems to have forged a hawkish coalition on the FOMC.
In fact, Pingle speculated that Warsh, following last week's post-meeting news conference, "left little doubt to us that his views more closely align" with Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, arguably one of the most hawkish of this year's voting group, "than anyone else on the FOMC."
For now, at least, markets are going with the interpretation that Warsh will let the Treasury market guide him toward progressively higher benchmark rates.
"There's a good reason why central bankers are beginning to be concerned about overheating in the investment section of the economy," said Brusuelas, the RSM economist. "Mr. Market is signaling something to policymakers like Kevin Warsh that they ought to listen to."

iOS 27 adds a variety of new features and changes for Apple Wallet, including one that’s been on my wishlist for years: the ability to import physical passes.
Apple Wallet offers a host of features to help you replace your physical wallet and keys.
It holds credit cards, driver’s licenses, transit cards, boarding passes, event tickets, car keys, home keys, hotel keys, and more.
And with iOS 27, the Wallet app takes another big step toward being the only wallet you need.
That’s because you can now import physical passes, tickets, membership cards, and the like into Apple Wallet.
Here’s how it works, per Apple :
iPhone and Apple Watch users will be able to create and store passes in Apple Wallet from physical cards, like loyalty or membership cards, eliminating the need to fumble through pockets and bags. With Siri mode in the Camera app, users simply point their iPhone at any physical card with a barcode or even screenshot a digital one, and they’ll be prompted to save it to Apple Wallet. Users can also create and add a pass directly from Apple Wallet. Once added, passes are ready to present as a barcode or QR code right from their iPhone or Apple Watch.
Digital passes are a lot more common today than when Apple Wallet first launched. But they aren’t available for everything.
I definitely still encounter businesses and events that utilize physical passes exclusively. And when I do, it adds a little anxiety to my life because I then need to remember to bring those passes with me at the right time.
But with iOS 27, everything can start going in the Wallet app, which is always with me. By putting everything in Wallet, the mental burden of remembering to bring something extra is suddenly gone.
Are there any physical passes you’ve added to Apple Wallet in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

That pretty much summed up an ugly Thursday night game in Wisconsin, the Falcons steamrolling the Packers 35-14 for their first win of the season as QB Michael Penix Jr. made his 2026 debut. Atlanta, which had 16 points all season entering the game, rolled off 27 in a row at one point in a runaway that immediately restored them to relevance in the NFC South. The Pack, meanwhile − still without injured superstar OLB Micah Parsons and Pro Bowl RB Josh Jacobs, among others − moved into the basement of the NFC North with a 1-2 record that somehow seems far more problematic than Atlanta’s.
The scoreboard said plenty, but there were quite a few other winners and losers Thursday, and they are as follows:
The Falcons quarterback, and team’s highly scrutinized first-round pick from 2024, started his first game in nearly a year after sufficiently recovering from the third ACL reconstruction of his football career, dating back to his college days. He threw an interception while getting reacclimated on his first drive, but ultimately completed 18 of 25 throws for 256 yards and a TD. His connection with WR Drake London certainly seemed fully intact, the duo hooking up nine times for 194 yards. Playing on a Thursday night also confers another benefit to Penix, who now gets 11 days to recover and gauge how his body responds with Atlanta scheduled to next play Oct. 5 in New Orleans, Week 4’s Monday nighter.
In the depths of their 0-2 start , the Falcons entered the game with nary a touchdown in the previous seven quarters – and just one all season – and had not played a snap in the opposition red-zone in 2026, a dry spell no team had experienced through its first two games since 2008. Thursday, they scored four touchdowns in five visits inside Green Bay's 20-yard line.
Y’all remember he’s a two-time NFL Coach of the Year, right? That seems to get obscured a bit after the rocky end to his six-year tenure with the Cleveland Browns – where all tenures end rockily – and was certainly accentuated by Atlanta’s ghastly start to this season. But if Penix didn’t completely unlock Stefanski’s offense, which did rack up a gaudy 498 yards, he certainly stabilized it and provided ample hope that the Falcons could still be a contender for the divisional throne this season. After notching his first win as Atlanta's HC, Stefanski is also now 6-0 on Thursday nights … 41-60 (playoffs included) during the rest of the week.
Maybe the lone silver lining for the Green and Gold, the fifth-year receiver continues to show what he's capable of when healthy, which has been the biggest obstacle to date during his career. Watson's first-quarter TD catch, which staked Green Bay to an early lead, was his fourth of the season, tying him for the league lead − albeit with one more game under his belt than Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Detroit's Amon-Ra St. Brown.
It's been a rough year-plus for the Atlanta defensive coordinator, even more so off the field than on. In 2025, Ulbrich's son infamously prank-called then-Colorado QB Shedeur Sanders as he tumbled into the third day of the draft, embarrassing the family and lightening the coach's wallet. This year has been much worse, Ulbrich's wife losing her battle with cancer in July. An inspired defensive effort against the Packers − and with the Falcons down several key starters due to injuries and pass rusher James Pearce Jr.'s suspension − only counts for so much, but it's nice to see something go right for the NFL lifer given all he's been through on a personal level.
As you’d expect, Bijan Robinson provided plenty of mustard to the Falcons offense, rushing for 194 yards and two scores. However he also got some nice backup from RB2 Brian Robinson Jr. (no relation), who chipped in with 50 yards and a score of his own.
Boy, do the Packers miss Jacobs – to say nothing of the legitimacy he provides to the play-action approach coach Matt LaFleur favored in 2025, a strategy that was obviously dead in the water against Atlanta ... yet curiously employed on fourth-and-1 from the Falcons' 7-yard line on the Packers' first possession of the second half. (The play failed miserably.) After averaging a meager 64.5 yards on the ground in their first two games, the Pack were far more ineffectual Thursday – producing all of 17 yards, among the lowest totals in the storied franchise's history. And with no return in sight for Jacobs, who remains on the commissioner’s exempt list – not to mention a battered O-line that was missing LG Aaron Banks and RT Zach Bako-Bewele, who’s out for the season with a knee injury – little reason to believe matters will improve any time soon.
The leader of the Pack on the field and at the bank – with a contract averaging $55 million annually – Love understandably continues to struggle trying to operate an offense that’s completely out of kilter while attempting to compensate for a defense that’s been grated for at least 35 points twice in three weeks. Aside from the lopsided pass-run ratio (54 dropbacks vs. nine rushes on Thursday), Love was also navigating his new blocking combination without injured WR Jayden Reed. While his position and paycheck put the onus on him, Love, who’s barely completing 50% of his passes this season − despite 312 empty-calorie yards and two TDs through the air Thursday − continues to be stuck in what’s presently a very unenviable position.
"I think a lot of areas we need to improve. But at the end of the day, I'll just sit here and look at myself and say there's so much stuff I can improve on to make us as an offense better," Love said afterward. "It always starts with me. To be the leader of the team, I've got to improve and be better in a lot of areas. There's a lot of stuff that I'll look at on film that I won't be happy with how I performed tonight."
There shouldn't be too much blame assessed to the Packers pass rusher. But we can't ignore that his roughing penalty on Penix late in the first quarter − when the Packers were leading 7-0 − kept the Falcons on the field following what appeared to be a failed third down. Bijan Robinson escaped for a 55-yard run on the next play, was in the end zone two snaps later, and the Falcons never looked back. Oops.
If you took the Falcons' Kyle Pitts or Packers' Tucker Kraft with an early pick in your fantasy draft ... bummer. They've combined for 11 receptions, none for TDs ... all season.
Unless Penix gets reinjured − sadly, his history suggests it will happen − the Dolphins castoff ain't playing extensively here. Expected to start in Week 1 before he injured an oblique muscle in practice , Tagovailoa's best bet to rekindle his career in 2026 might entail a release from his one-year deal or a trade to a quarterback-needy team, say the New York Giants potentially?
Arguably the most iconic stadium in the NFL , it’s been privy to a lot of good football in recent decades – and most certainly on opening night. But not Thursday. The loss to the previously winless and inept Falcons was not only embarrassing and frustrating for the locals, it also ended the Packers’ streak of winning 13 consecutive home openers.

articles.title_orig: Woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her aged 13 says claims were false
articles.title_zh: Woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her aged 13 says claims were false
articles.content_orig:
Unnamed woman who filed and later dropped lawsuit against rap superstar states that she never met him, contrary to initial allegation of 2000 assault
A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 years old has formally withdrawn her allegation, saying that she has never met the rap superstar.
The unnamed woman had originally made the allegation in a lawsuit filed in 2024, claiming that Jay-Z , real name Shawn Carter, had drugged and raped her with Sean Combs, known as P Diddy. The incident was alleged to have happened at a party after an MTV awards ceremony in 2000.
Jay-Z denied the allegations, describing them as a blackmail attempt, and Combs also denied them. Jay-Z’s lawyer maintained the events relied on an “impossible timeline”. The woman dropped the lawsuit in 2025 , and Jay-Z filed a counter suit .
As that lawsuit progresses, the woman has now said her claims were false. “Shawn ‘Jay-Z’ Carter never raped me. I have never met or spoken to Mr Carter. Mr Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever,” she said in a declaration obtained by Rolling Stone .
She added that there was “no truth to any of my claims against Mr Carter. I understand my false accusations have caused Mr Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone.”
The woman has now been dropped from Jay-Z’s lawsuit, though the rapper is still pursuing her former lawyers, claiming they should have known the allegations were “contradicted by publicly available information, internally inconsistent, and unsupported by any credible story or investigation”. Earlier this month, as they made a motion to have the lawsuit dismissed, lawyer Tony Buzbee and his co-counsel described it as “a malicious prosecution”.
Regarding the woman’s new statement, Buzbee told Rolling Stone: “If for some reason now she is claiming she lied to us and the court, that’s new information.”
The woman’s current lawyer, James Blair Newman Jr, said: “Our client maintains that she was a victim of sexual assault, but she was entirely mistaken in her allegations identifying Mr Carter.”
Continuing her statement, the woman said memories of sexual assault were triggered by seeing an advertisement calling for victims of Combs to come forward. Combs was being investigated for a number of alleged sexual assaults, and – unrelated to the unnamed woman’s case – was eventually found guilty on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution, receiving a four year and two month sentence in October 2025.
The woman said that after making the allegations, she was unaware of the lawsuit being filed on her behalf and, after she expressed doubts about her claims, the lawsuit was dropped.
Jay-Z has previously spoken about the impact the allegations had on his life. When the case was dropped, he said: “The trauma that my wife, my children, loved ones and I have endured can never be dismissed,” and speaking to GQ in March he said: “I haven’t been that angry in a long time, uncontrollable anger. You don’t put that on someone – that’s a thing that you better be super sure [about].”
He said he had refused to settle the lawsuit out of court: “ I can’t take a settlement – it ain’t in my DNA … I would die .”

articles.title_orig: Details on U.S.-China trade negotiations coming Monday, USTR Greer says
articles.title_zh: Details on U.S.-China trade negotiations coming Monday, USTR Greer says
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that the U.S. and China have reached agreements covering a subset of goods the two countries can trade on more favorable terms, marking fresh progress in negotiations between the world's two largest economies.
"We've actually reached agreement with the Chinese on a number of these things," Greer said on CNBC's "Squawk Box," referring to goods including U.S. agricultural products and medical devices and Chinese consumer goods considered non-sensitive.
Greer said the Trump administration plans to release "a lot more details" Monday about what the two sides have accomplished in negotiations over the past several weeks. He said the goal is to carve out areas of trade that could remain insulated from future tariff measures or broader trade disputes.
The two countries want some goods to be traded on a "more preferential basis" and potentially left aside if either country imposes new tariffs.
Greer did not specify Friday which products are covered by the agreements, how tariffs on those goods could change or when the new terms would take effect. Negotiations under the new U.S.-China "Board of Trade" mechanism are focused on "pure trade issues," Greer said, rather than U.S. national security restrictions on advanced technology.
"All those export controls that are national security issues, we take those off the table," Greer said.
Trump and Xi, after they met in Beijing in May, announced the establishment of the "Board of Trade" to manage trade between the two rivals in non-sensitive products. Businesses have been waiting for more details on what categories of trade would be set aside, under the new framework, for lower tariffs.
The news come as Washington and Beijing have also agreed to extend their broader trade truce by two months, giving the two sides more time to negotiate over longstanding economic disputes.
Greer said Friday that the U.S. views those two months as "compliance periods" to assess whether China is following through on earlier commitments, including purchases of U.S. soybeans and other agricultural products and access to rare earths needed by American manufacturers.
"Whenever we have these compliance periods that roll over, it's a time for us to assess, reassess and determine whether or not to continue this period of relative peace on the economic front with the Chinese," Greer said.
Meanwhile, tariffs have sharply altered U.S. trade flows . Greer said Friday that the U.S. goods trade deficit with China has fallen nearly 40%, while acknowledging that some trade has shifted to other countries as companies adjust their supply chains.
Mexico has been one beneficiary of that shift. U.S. imports from Mexico reached a record $60.6 billion in July, according to the Census Bureau . The seasonally adjusted U.S. goods deficit with Mexico increased by $7.2 billion that month to $27.5 billion, according to the Census Bureau.
"When you impose tariffs ... you see market actors starting to do what market actors do, which is respond to new terms of trade, respond to new incentives in the market," Greer said. "We're actually seeing a lot come back to North America."
Greer's comments also provided new detail from the U.S. side following Trump's meeting with Xi at the White House on Thursday. Beijing has so far released a more detailed public account of the talks than Washington.
Xi told Trump on Thursday that artificial intelligence presents greater opportunities for U.S.-China cooperation than competition, according to a Chinese state media readout.
"The two sides can continue AI dialogue, exchange views on risks and benefits, and together guard against the misuse or malicious use of AI," Xi said, according to a CNBC translation of the readout .
Trump, in a Truth Social post Friday morning, called the meeting with Xi "very productive" and said the Chinese leader appeared receptive to Trump's preferred term of "SUPER INTELLIGENCE" for artificial intelligence.
"Tremendous things will be happening," Trump wrote.

articles.title_orig: Wisconsin police find dozens of partially clothed men in frat house basement in alleged hazing incident
articles.title_zh: Wisconsin police find dozens of partially clothed men in frat house basement in alleged hazing incident
articles.content_orig:
Two 20-year-olds were arrested after police were called to the scene of an alleged hazing incident where over two dozen young men were partially clothed and covered in liquids. Some of them were injured, police said.
The Madison Police Department said they received an anonymous tip about an event at the unaccredited Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity. When they arrived at the house, they found about 30 "partially clothed males covered in food, condiments and other liquids" in the basement. The room's thermostat was set to 81 degrees, police said.
Several of the men had "visible injuries consistent with being abused," police said.
The "vast majority" of the men were 18, police said.
A photo with the men's faces redacted shows the group in a dirty space with black walls and the Alpha Epsilon Pi letters painted on a piece of furniture.
Two people, identified by police as Brayden J. Klein and Samuel N. Vane, were arrested for hazing and disorderly conduct and taken to the Dane County Jail. The Madison Police Department said that the president and vice president of the fraternity were present and spoke to responding officers, but did not specify if Klein and Vane held those titles.
The men in the basement were escorted outside and checked for incapacitation and injuries.
"Several of these men had visible injuries consistent with being physically assaulted," police said.
No other charges have been announced in relation to the incident. An investigation remains ongoing, and those with information are asked to contact the Madison Police Department.
Alpha Epsilon Pi is an unrecognized and unaccredited student organization at the University of Wisconsin, police and the school said. It was suspended at the school in 2013 after a 17-year-old and another person were taken to detox after being served alcohol at a party hosted by the fraternity, the Associated Press reported, citing university records. The fraternity was terminated after a fourth incident involving either events, alcohol or both, and since 2016, there have been seven additional allegations related to intramural sports, disrespectful behavior, drinking and hazing.
The school said in a statement that because the chapter is still recognized by the national Alpha Epsilon Pi organization, it is legally allowed to operate as an unaffiliated fraternity chapter.
A spokesperson for the Alpha Epsilon Pi Headquarters said it takes the allegations concerning the Madison chapter "extremely seriously." The national organization plans to "cooperate fully" with the investigation, the spokesperson said, and members found responsible for criminal conduct will be expelled from the organization.
"Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for," the spokeperson said." There is no place for it in AEPi. No exceptions. No excuses. We educate our members about their responsibility to 'Be Your Brothers' Keeper.' This is not an optional value. It is a fundamental expectation of membership. Anyone who engages in hazing forfeits the privilege of being an AEPi brother."
The University of Wisconsin said it is also investigating the incident as it relates to its nonacademic misconduct process. Campus officials are providing support to affected students.
The Madison Police Department said that anyone whose safety is jeopardized during the Greek life recruitment process should contact authorities.

In a surprise nod to shared history, US President Donald Trump called China a World War II ally as he welcomed Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday ahead of summit talks.
“If we focus on our common interests, I’m confident there is much we can achieve,” Trump said in the White House foyer during the state welcome ceremony ahead of formal talks with the Chinese president.

articles.title_orig: Bond Yields at 5% Mark New Era 'Until Something Breaks'
articles.title_zh: Bond Yields at 5% Mark New Era 'Until Something Breaks'
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Treasury yields inched higher on Friday as recent selling pressure intensified following hawkish Fed commentary and stronger-than-expected economic data.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury note was up more than 2 basis points to 5.183% after reaching its highest rate since June 2007 on Thursday. The 30-year Treasury bond was higher by more than 1 basis point at 5.476% after surging to levels not seen since 2004. The 2-year note yield was up less than 1 basis point at 4.901%.
One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
Investors weighed a global bond selloff this week as Japanese government bonds, U.K. gilts, German bunds and other eurozone bonds hit fresh highs. Eurozone and Japanese government bond yields edged lower on Friday.
Treasury yields have been driven higher by hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr, who said in a speech on Wednesday that "further policy adjustments" can be expected to bring inflation down to target. Other factors included stubbornly high oil prices and the purchasing managers' index report hitting its highest level in more than four years.
Traders were last pricing in a 66% chance of a rate hike in October, according to the CME FedWatch tool .
On Friday, the Commerce Department reported that durable goods orders in August were relatively unchanged. Economists polled by Dow Jones had expected a decline of 0.3%.
"Ahead, we think that there are enough rate hike fears discounted at this juncture, and certainly enough to take care of perceived inflation risks," ING's regional head of research for the Americas Padhraic Garvey and senior rates strategist Benjamin Schroeder wrote in a note on Friday.
"But, government bond yields are primed to remain under pressure on a pure debt dynamic theory, which translates into pressure for some re-widening in swap spreads, and especially in the 10yr area."
